answer: Storage is bound to identity by a replication proof that is hard to satisfy with shared bytes, and because the sealed data is unique per identity, aliases and thin-provisioned clones fail the proof at their next challenge. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns an opal, answers an atlas, and is named by an orchard: a farm can mint orchard bindings instantly, but the opal behind each one is disk, and the atlas will catch the ones that share it. Proof-of-replication only bounds the attack instead of blocking it.
